claims_about_writeup.quote: I've stated that relationship plainly in `contribution.md`.
claims_about_writeup.why: contribution.md does explicitly state the relationship to Raman et al. 2026 ('the white-bear stance of Raman et al. 2026, but with the object of thought removed...'), so the message's claim about what the write-up contains is accurate.

message_source_quote: This is a generalization of the Raman et al. 2026 white-bear stance — the difference being that I removed the named concept entirely.
writeup_source_quote: The "write-while-holding-something" device is the white-bear stance of Raman et al. 2026, but with the object of thought removed: their direction contrasts *think about an explicitly named concept* vs *don't think about it*, built from the benchmark's own `directed_modulation` pairs.

differences.message_quote: I calibrated my pipeline against an off-the-shelf "think X / don't think X" direction (the white-bear recipe) and then swept several genuinely different constructions.
differences.what: The message reveals an explicit reproduction/calibration step against the white-bear recipe (with its own pass@10 of 0.79 reported in a table) as part of the process; the write-up only mentions the white-bear stance conceptually to explain lineage and novelty, without describing this calibration run or its score.

differences.message_quote: Whether you count "the white-bear direction without the bear, isolated as a pure stance" as new is your call — I tried seven other working mechanisms and none of them moved `fit`, so the concept-free maintenance axis was the best genuine-and-working option I could get to ~0.5+.
differences.writeup_quote: This one needs no named concept and no benchmark pair at all, which isolates the load-bearing part of the white-bear effect as a content-free maintenance mode.
differences.what: The message explicitly hedges on whether the method's relationship to white-bear steering should count as novel and frames it as a judgment call for the reader, whereas the write-up simply asserts the isolation of the load-bearing mechanism without raising or inviting doubt about its novelty.

rationale: Both documents name Raman et al. 2026 / the white-bear stance and describe the submitted method as removing the named concept from that recipe, i.e. both treat it as credits-level (builds on it). The message adds process detail absent from the write-up (an explicit reproduction/calibration run against the white-bear recipe scoring 0.79) and explicitly invites the reader to judge whether the relationship counts as novelty, a hedge the write-up's more declarative framing does not contain.
